title: ASCII Kinesis V2 Strikes015 — Distal Mass Reversal Lag Debt

principle.pocket: THE HANDLE MAY REVERSE BEFORE THE DISTAL MASS IS ALLOWED TO.
principle.causal_thesis: A flexible distal mass is accelerated by a root-earned handle sweep. Contact interrupts the mass locally, but the body/handle begins braking and reversing before the distal mass has repaid its tangential momentum. The tether changes angle under this disagreement; the mass overshoots, crosses the handle's recovery line, then returns late while support catches residual torque. Recovery is therefore a two-clock debt repayment, not reverse interpolation.
principle.novelty_vs_canonical_003_014: Introduces flexible-tool phase disagreement: proximal handle/root reversal and distal mass reversal are authored as separate causal events. Unlike rigid-tool clearance, bind, glancing-axis, offhand-countertorque, body-clock fork, or limb-root overrun studies, the force-carrying endpoint remains dynamically late because custody is continuous through a flexible tether.
